notebooks.title: Architectural and Methodological Paths to Reasoning Transparency
notebooks.summary: Incorporating Structured Cognitive Loop findings to demonstrate how explicit control and externalized memory reduce unsupported assertions compared to prompt-based baselines.
notebooks.findings: Separating cognition, control, and memory in agent architectures reduces unsupported assertions and improves goal fidelity compared to standard prompt-based baselines. [source-51196608d740480b]
notebooks.limitations: Findings rely on specific multi-step agent scenarios and matched decoding settings; generalizing to arbitrary environments requires broader empirical testing.
notebooks.next_questions: Do PCFG-derived uncertainty metrics can autonomously trigger meta-reasoning loops in a test environment?
notebooks.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate new evidence on architectural separation of cognition and control.

notebooks.title: Flow-State as an Emergent Preference
notebooks.summary: Evidence suggests that users have a persistent, stable preference for 'flow' states. AI systems that prioritize this preference must minimize disruptive interventions, using control loops to verify whether an intervention actually supports or hinders the user's flow.
notebooks.findings:
Users exhibit a stable preference for tasks that balance difficulty and skill level, a state defined as 'flow', which AI interventions must avoid disrupting. [source-92051b5126f140f6]

Control loops are necessary to verify if automated interventions support the emergent preference for flow. [source-51196608d740480b]
notebooks.limitations: Flow is highly subjective and context-dependent; metrics for detecting it (e.g., typing hesitation) are noisy proxies and may vary significantly across user demographics.
notebooks.next_questions: How can we refine cross-modal behavioral cues to differentiate 'flow' from mere task-frustration?
notebooks.reason: Revising to integrate control-loop verification as a mechanism for validating user flow preferences.

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings on memory retention, stability-plasticity dilemmas, and catastrophic forgetting, focusing on how these factors influence stable preference anchoring in intelligent systems. The analysis highlights that managing the tradeoff between retaining past episodic experiences and adapting to new inputs remains a critical barrier to stable, autonomous preference formation.
